roleCompare: whole u32: input writes 1, output writes 2; new values only for new ends; no flag bits
containerFramingAcrossAbi: fixed: header length, chunk header, padding, chunk count meaning; migrations change payloads only

chunks.unknown: kept, written back after the known chunks in their original order

load.case: abi above this build, role of this end
load.note: original bytes kept by any setState and written back unchanged until a successfully loaded state replaces them

load.case: abi above this build, other role

layout: count x { u8 idLen, id, f32 value }
prms.trimDropsOnly: unknown PRMS ids, from the end

layout: repeat to end of payload: u16 key, u16 len, bytes[len]
cfgs.unknownKeys: kept, written back after the known keys in their original order

invariants.rule: a state is at least 16 bytes
the first 16 bytes (magic, abi, role, chunk count) never move or change meaning
role is compared as a whole u32: input writes 1, output writes 2
the container framing is fixed across abi
PRMS reads and writes share one limit: at most 256 entries and 65536 bytes
growing PRMS past these limits requires an abi bump, because the limits are part of the format
trimToDecodable before encoding drops only unknown PRMS ids, from the end, never a known parameter
a document from decodeDocument with nothing added always encodes
before the instance settles every successfully loaded state is applied in full, the last one wins
after it settles, later states only change parameters

settling happens at the first user action in the UI: a gesture-begun parameter edit, a setting edit in the UI, a manually picked group, confirming a takeover; host-sent values and automation do not count
no claim settles the instance, because a provisional claim is meant to be preempted by a later project state
known residue: an instance never touched in the UI still applies a host preset or A/B in full, group included
Empty, IgnoredProbe, Corrupt and RejectedNewer neither apply anything nor settle the instance
any setState that gets RejectedNewer for this role keeps the original bytes, regardless of call order
kept bytes stay until a successfully loaded state (Ok or Migrated) replaces them; a later RejectedNewer replaces them with its own bytes
parameter edits made while bytes are kept do not enter the state and are lost on save
